crime: Earlier that week, a girl had joined {WITCH_NAME} in a private performance in the reception room, taking the play’s second role. Today, encouraged by it, she used her phone in the lounge to invite the prisoners to a reading.

“You’ll only laugh at it,” {WITCH_NAME} told the prisoners. The girl handed one prisoner the private script anyway, giving them a copy to follow. In response, {WITCH_NAME} used her Magic to leave a living duplicate of herself in the lounge. While the duplicate kept the prisoner talking by improvising a hopeful ending to the play, {WITCH_NAME} fatally stabbed the girl in the chest with a sword in the reception room, before the reading began.

When the girl’s body was discovered in the reception room, that prisoner gave {WITCH_NAME} an alibi: the two had been talking continuously in the lounge. But during that conversation, the prisoner had bandaged the woman’s blistered right palm after a tea scald. Examining {WITCH_NAME}’s right palm now, the prisoner found uninjured skin. That mismatch unraveled the alibi: the prisoner had been talking to {WITCH_NAME}’s living duplicate.
fields.epitaph: Certain they would laugh, she ended the story before she could learn whether they might welcome her.
fields.epithet: The Storyteller Who Swallowed Her Words
execution: The execution stand clamps her inside a puppet stage with a troupe of marionettes in her likeness. The marionettes lower a bladed curtain through her neck, then bow before her severed head in a final curtain call.

magic.name: Second Selves
magic.text: Create living copies of yourself, each with an independent mind and will.
